utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Ms. Fikirini? Your next witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Our next witness will be Lulzim Vejsa. But before we proceed, the Prosecution would like to request for a change of mode of testimony. The witness was initially earmarked to be a live witness and we would like him to come as 92 ter witness, which was formerly known as 89(F) witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration to tell the truth by reading aloud the document which will now be placed before you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Your Honour, this witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just hold on a second while I get to grips with the changing situation. Do we have a copy of the statement that will be part of the witness's evidence?

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And is that a statement which is --

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: That's the statement --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- dated at least of an interview of the 15th and 16th of April, 1999?

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. And what you propose is that you will invite the witness to adopt that statement as an accurate account of events in the course of his evidence?

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Yes, your honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And that's you applying Rule 89(F).

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: When you make that application, which will no doubt be in a moment or two, if anyone sees any reason to object to that, no doubt they will alert me; and if no one does, then it will become part of the process in the usual way. So please continue with your examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Vejsa. Could you please state your full name, please.

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: Good morning. Lulzim Vejsa.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Mr. Vejsa, did you provide a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor on the 15th and 16th of April, 1999, concerning events that you experienced and witnessed in Kosovo in 1999?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: And, Mr. Vejsa, did you have an opportunity to review your statement recently?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: And from that review, were you satisfied that the contents of this statement accurately reflect, to the best of your knowledge and recollection, the truth about the events that you describe in that statement?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Your Honour, I wish to tender this witness's statement as Exhibit P2350.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I just have a procedural inquiry. Apparently Your Honours have this statement, and I'm wondering how, when the application is just made at this moment, that that statement was provided to you in what was to be a live witness. I thought that matter had been dealt with and they were not to provide you with any statements other than those that were 92 bis, 89(F), whatever. I'm just wondering how that happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I'm trying to work that out myself, Mr. -- ah. I see now something I had overlooked on this. When the application to revoke the protective measures was made, there was a note, "We also propose to change his mode of testimony from viva voce to Rule 92 ter or old Rule 89(F). He will adopt his April 1999 ICTY statement for this purpose, and we will lead him briefly on a few matters to expand or clarify." Now, that's the standard practice that is followed where -- but you are right; that, strictly speaking, where there is a change of this nature, it rather pre-empts your opportunity to take exception. I hope, though, when this sort of thing happens you'll trust us to exclude from our minds any material that ultimately is not admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I fully do, Your Honour. I just remember a little earlier, several days ago where you said that you had instructed the Prosecution not to give you statements unless this situation --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's quite right. But I suspect and I'm sure that nothing inappropriate was intended here. And I see no objection to the statement coming from any counsel, so therefore no harm is done. But it's a timely reminder of the procedure to be followed. Carry on, please, Ms. Fikirini.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Mr. Vejsa, on page 2 of your statement, you describe that on the 31st of March, 1999, your wife went to inquire from two Serb women if there was any way you could leave town. My question is: Do you know the name of the first Serb woman your wife visited? If you remember?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: Yes. I do. The first woman -- I remember her name, Hrtsava [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: And do you know where that woman was living?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: Yes. She was living very close to us.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Can you approximate the distance from your house to that woman's house?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: Approximately 15 to 20 metres away from my house.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: And what did your wife tell you when she came back after visiting this woman?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: My wife told me that this neighbour, this woman, told her, "Don't be frightened. If your husband is not involved with the KLA, don't be afraid. Stay at your home. You don't need to leave." This was all.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: And you also described in your statement that your wife also went to visit the wife of the chief of the MUP of Gjakova to inquire on the same thing. Did your wife tell you what she was told by that woman, the second Serb woman who is the wife of chief of MUP of Gjakova?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: Yes. The same words as the other woman, and as a matter of fact, she said more convincing words, "Don't be afraid. My husband is in the police. You don't have to be frightened."

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: And how far is your house to this second woman's house, or to the chief of MUP of Gjakova?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: There are three houses between our houses. So probably 20 to 25 metres from my house.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Prior to this day, the 31st of March, 1999, did you happen to know these two women?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: And did you also happen to know the chief of the MUP of Gjakova?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Do you know his name?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: Yes. Novak Pitolic.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this point I would like to use Exhibit P276.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Mr. Vejsa, can you see a photograph which is in front of you?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Do you recognise that photograph? Or can you say anything in relation to the photograph which you're seeing in front of you?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: Yes. This is my house. My house is in this picture.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Okay. Using a pen -- can I get usher's assistance, please? Using a pen, would you please indicate on the map where your house is -- on that photograph, sorry.

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: Yes, here.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Can you mark it as number 1, please.

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: [Marks]. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: How many houses did you have?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: Two houses. One of them was bigger than the other. The second house is here.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: And you just told us a few minutes ago that the first Serb woman was living about 20, 15 metres from your house. Can you also show in that photograph where that first Serb woman's house is?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: You cannot see it here in this photograph but it was somewhere here.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Okay. Can you write a proper 3 so that we can know that it goes into that direction and also maybe draw an arrow indicating that the house is in that direction.

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Okay. And also from this photograph, are you able to see the house which belonged to the second Serb woman or which belonged to the chief of the MUP of the Gjakova?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Mr. Vejsa --

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like this photograph to be left there for a moment because I will come back to it.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Mr. Vejsa, after your wife told you what she was told by these two Serb women, how did you and your family feel?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: We felt much safer.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: And in your statement, Mr. Vejsa, you describe the events which took place on the 1st and 2nd of April, and you stated that you fled away and come back the next morning. When you came back the next morning, did you go to your house?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: Not to my house, because we saw that it had been burned. And in front of the house there were three Serb policemen.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: How did you know that there were three Serb policemen? How did you know that those people were police?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: We saw them in front of my house and they were wearing uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: When you're saying they were wearing uniform, can you describe what kind of uniform were they wearing?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: Yes. They were wearing police uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: And let us now go back to the photograph. Can you mark on the photograph which you have marked earlier where those three policemen were standing?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: And do you remember the uniform which they were wearing, if -- I mean the colour and if it has any pattern?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court, please.

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: Yes. It was blue.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Solid blue, blue camouflage? What kind of blue?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: No. It was solid, normal, without any camouflage.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: You saw that your house has been burnt down. You couldn't go there. Where did you go?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: We went to my aunt's house.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: And where is your aunt's house?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: Here, in between these two houses.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this point I will ask if a snapshot of this photograph could be taken and an IC number given to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be IC51, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: In your statement, you also described or stated that from what had happened, you and other relatives of yours, joined a convoy which was heading to Albania and on your way you went through two check-points. My question is: When you came across the first check-point, do you remember who was manning that check-point?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: Yes. When we went to the first check-point, there were policemen there.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Are these the -- do you remember what they were wearing?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Could you describe what was their uniform like?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: Yes. They were wearing police uniforms as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Are these uniforms the same as those which were worn by the three policemen who were guarding or standing in front of your house?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: And at the second check-point, do you remember who was manning this second check-point?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: Yes. The army was there.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: How did you know that these were army?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: Army forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: How did you know that?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: Because of the uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Yeah. Were these uniforms different from those which you described were worn by the police?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Can you describe those uniforms, then?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: Yes. These were green uniforms, camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: And from that second check-point, you then crossed into Albania. Do you remember the name of that border crossing?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: I can't remember it for the moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: But you remember crossing into Albania from Kosovo, do you?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I think it was called Krume, the first place.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Mr. Vejsa, if you won't mind, I will take you back. When you told us that you saw three policemen standing in front of your house, were you able to recognise any of those? Any one of them?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: Yes. The three of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Yes. Can you tell us, please --

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Yeah. Can you give us their names, if you know them by names?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: Yes. One of them was Lubisa, he was a neighbour here; he lived 20 metres away. The other one, Novica lives on the other street; he's also 20 metres away from where I live. The third one I think was Lubisa's brother, Nenad.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Your Honour, can we please get back Exhibit P276? With a fresh page, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Mr. Vejsa, using your pen -- usher, would you please assist? Using the pen, can you please explain or show us where the first policeman you named as Lubisa lived?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: Lubisa. You know, I spoke about the first woman where my wife went?

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: So it's approximately here where he lived.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: And where was the second policeman living?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: The second policeman lived on the other street, because here it divides into two streets, somewhere here.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: And the third one?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: The third one lived together with the first one. They were brothers, Lubisa and Nenad.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we can get a snapshot of this and an IC number, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be IC52, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Vejsa, do you have a job nowadays?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I work now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What is it you do?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. O'Sullivan.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, the order will be General Lukic, General Pavkovic, General Lazarevic, General Ojdanic, Mr. Sainovic and Mr. Milutinovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Good morning, sir. My name is Dan Ivetic, and I'm one of the attorneys representing Mr. Sreten Lukic relative to this trial. I'm assisted by Branko Lukic and Mr. Ozren Ogrizovic in that task today. I'm going to have to ask you a few questions to clarify and better understand your testimony, so please bear with me and try to listen to my questions so that you can give me the most accurate and concise answers possible. My first question has to deal with something you mentioned at the beginning of your written statement to the Office of the Prosecutor. With the situation in the town of Djakovica prior to the NATO bombings, is it accurate to state that the burning of shops that you describe in the beginning of your statement did not commence until after NATO started bombing Kosovo-Metohija. That is to say, that there were no such incidents before the NATO bombings?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: No. There were no incidents before. These happened the day when the NATO bombing started.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. And with respect to these shops, I just wanted to clarify and make sure I have the correct information. Is it accurate that you did not actually see how these shops were set on fire? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: Yes. That's correct. I did not see but I could see the smoke and the flames because it's approximately 150 metres away from my house and you could see everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, since we are interested in what's -- in other things that occurred in Djakovica in this trial, I'm going to ask you a couple of questions to try and clarify some background points before we get to the unfortunate incidents relating to your relatives. Now, first of all, I know, and we have your statement and so I know that you state you were never a member of the UCK/KLA, but I want to ask you as a resident of Djakovica if you had occasion to see or hear about the presence of the KLA in Djakovica or the surrounding villages?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: It is true that I was not a member of the KLA, but I had heard about them, that there were such people in the villages and town.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you recall hearing at any time either in 1998 or 1999 of any attacks carried out by the KLA within the municipality, and that is to say within either Djakovica town or the surrounding villages?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: No. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, sir. And now I'd like to ask you also about the neighbourhood where you lived in the city. First of all, before the NATO bombings started, what were the relations like between you and your Serbian neighbours, if you can answer that?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: Yes. We had very good relations with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did those relations change in any way after the NATO bombings started?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: Yes. These relations changed immediately after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And could you describe for us, did they change for the better or for the worse or -- any information you can provide about that would be helpful?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: Of course for the worse.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And in particular, these three neighbours that you have identified, Lubisa, Lubisa's brother, and I believe the third individual is Novica, in particular, how did the relations change with respect to them?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: Well, from what I heard, from my first neighbour, he saw these policemen and some others whose names I don't remember. He saw them involved in my particular case, that they were involved in the crime.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Prior to that case, prior to that incident, had you had any other bad relations with these families?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And if we could step back to the time-period before the war, I'd like to ask you specifically about these three individuals. Do you know whether they were active policemen before the war, these three individuals, Lubisa, Novica, and Lubisa's brother for whom we don't have a name?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: They were police reservists. They were mobilised.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you know approximately when they were mobilised?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. So at some point in time during that time-period; is that correct? You don't know the specific -- you can't give us any more specific of a time-period, can you?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: No, not the month.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, what can you tell me about the NATO air strikes in the Djakovica region? Do you have any personal knowledge or did you hear of any sites within Djakovica municipality that were bombed by the NATO forces?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: For the period I was in Gjakova, that is from the 24th of March when the bombing started and up until 2nd of April, I heard that only the military barracks were bombed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Did you hear about any civilian casualties resulting from the bombing of the military barracks or any other bombings by NATO in the Djakovica region?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: There were no casualties caused by NATO, victims, I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And after NATO started its bombing campaign in Kosovo-Metohija, is it accurate to state that during that time the electricity in Djakovica was off from time to time? That there were outages of electricity?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: Yes. We had electricity throughout the day, and in the evening at around 7.00 p.m., the electricity would go off until the morning hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And when the electricity would go off, how would residents, specifically how would your family, how would lighting be provided in the home dwelling?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: We would stay without electricity, without light. We would use candles.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, drawing your attention specifically to the night of April 1st to the morning of April 2nd, 1999, do you recall whether there was an electricity outage in your neighbourhood or in your home on that evening?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: Yes. Just like every other night, the electricity went off at 7.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And on the evening of April the 2nd, appears I misspoke, on the evening of April the 2nd, was this also the case?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: On the 2nd of April, I wasn't there in the evening. I was on my way to Albania.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. So -- and the critical night when the people came to knock on your door, the electricity was out at that time. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: Yes. That's correct. There was no electricity.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Were -- was your family using lit candles at that point in time, when the persons came and knocked on the door?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: No. They were sleeping, all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, is it accurate that the family members that were staying in the basement -- and we are talking about I believe the basement of the pool hall; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Those family members had been in the basement for a couple of days already by then, sleeping in the basement a couple days. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: During the day, we would stay in the first house, the big one, and during the night, women and children would go to the basement, to sleep.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And was that due to the threat posed by NATO bombs?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: No, not by NATO bombs. But the Serb forces were at Cabrat, and we were scared.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if we can focus on the actual time when the -- when this event began at your home. First of all, you state in your statement that men came knocking at the door on the early morning hours of April the 2nd. What I would like to know is at -- at that time I presume it was still dark outside; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: Yes. It was still dark outside. It was 12.15, just after midnight.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And then these men that came knocking, did they come only to your lot or home, or did they also go to other yards in the neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: Before they came to my house, in the same neighbourhood, they started to knock on the doors of two other houses and they started to torch the houses. Later, my brother-in-law came. He woke us up. He came to the big house where we were staying, and he said to us that someone was coming towards our direction and that we had to leave. Two or three minutes later, we heard the shoutings of the police. They were calling on us, and through a window behind the house, we escaped, we jumped a wall after wall and arrived at about 50 metres far from my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, is it correct that you did not actually see the persons who were calling for you and shouting before going out the window?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: No. Personally I didn't see them. My brother-in-law saw them.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And did he describe the type of uniforms that they were wearing for you to make the distinction that they were Serb policemen and paramilitaries or is that something that you're relying upon his identification for?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: My brother-in-law did not describe their uniforms to me. He just told me that they were torching houses and that they were approaching our gate.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Did you have occasion to recognise anyone's voice of the people that were shouting?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: No. At that moment, we were going outside from the backside of my house. We were escaping.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And with respect to while you were escaping, did you at that time see any of the individuals who were shouting, knocking on doors or torching houses?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And just so that we are clear, your sister's husband, your brother-in-law that you mentioned, that's Behar that we are talking about. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: Yes, Behar.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, in your -- first of all, that evening -- strike that. The next morning, you state that you were walking home and saw that houses in the district were burned. Am I correct that you did not actually see any of these houses being started on fire at any point in time? That is to say they were already burnt when you saw them that next morning?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: When we returned that morning, the houses were burnt.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I'd like to focus a little bit on these three individuals, these three neighbours that you have described as police reservists. You said that they were wearing uniforms. Could you please tell us whether the uniforms were one piece or whether they were wearing any type of vest over the uniforms?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: They were just wearing a police uniform, the uniform of the reservists. Without the vest, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, how long did these three individuals stay guarding your house, if you know, that morning?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: I would say I saw them only for three or four minutes that morning, while we were passing by in the column. And one of them, Lubisa, said to me, "You see, Lulzim, what NATO did to us?" And I had no strength to reply to that. I just continued my own journey.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did they -- did these three individuals appear to be inebriated or drunk at the time?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: No, they didn't appear drunk. But at the window of my shop, of the pool hall, while passing through there, I could see bottles of liquor. I could see injections on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: When you said you could see injections on the ground, are you talking about syringes?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I take it that you did not store syringes in the -- in the shop prior to this instance; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: No. My shop was a pool hall. There I was selling spirits and soft drinks.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I think we are in agreement and understanding. I just want to clarify. What I'm saying is that the syringes could not have come from your shop; they had to have been brought there by somebody else. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: Those syringes were used by your police. My shop was not a clinic or something else, if that's what you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No, that's exactly the opposite of what I mean. I'm trying to get the same point that I think you've answered. When you say "your police," are you talking about these three individuals, your neighbours, Lubisa, Novica, and Lubisa's brother, just so we are clear?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: It wasn't only these three that were at my house that night. As I mentioned earlier, my neighbour went on the top floor of his house and he saw that there were more than three persons there. In front of my shop they were drinking, they were taking drugs, and then they entered my house and committed the crime over my family.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, I thank you for your testimony and your time, and I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Aleksic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. We have no questions for this witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Lazarevic Defence doesn't have any questions for this witness either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Sepenuk.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: No questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Fila.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, no questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: No questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Fikirini.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I have two or three questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: Mr. Vejsa, when you were coming back the next morning, was your house the only house which was burnt on Millosh Giliq Street?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: No. There were other houses too.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: And you had been asked about the NATO bombing. Do you know or had you heard about NATO bombing your neighbourhood on that night of the 1st to the 2nd of April?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: What about from the 24th of March, when NATO bombing started?

utterances.speaker: LULZIM VEJSA
utterances.text: No. Not in my neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: MS. FIKIRINI
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, Mr. Vejsa, that completes your evidence. Thank you very much for coming to the Tribunal to give that evidence, and you're now free to leave.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Ms. Moeller.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the next witness is Mr. Isuf Zhuniqi. And I will swap places with Ms. Fikirini.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you help us with the paragraph numbers for this witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Mr. Zhuniqi is the first of a group of six witnesses which is coming now which addresses the municipality of Orahovac, and he specifically talks about a murder incident in paragraph 75(b) and Schedule B. His evidence is also relevant to paragraph 72(a)(i) and 72(a), as well as paragraphs 25 to 32 and 77(a),(b) and (d).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Your Honours, while the witness is brought in, may I also inform you that there is one more witness who is going to address this particular murder incident charged in paragraph 75(b) in the indictment and who will testify live. He was scheduled to come this week, but unfortunately due to a family emergency he couldn't come this week, so he will come later and will be led live about this incident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is he one of the witnesses on the list for this week?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: No, he's not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: This is just meant to explain why we called a 92 bis -- formerly a 92 bis (D) witness, who is now a 92 ter witness before we could call the live witness. We would have preferred to do it the other way around. To give you the full story.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Zhuniqi.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration to tell the truth by reading aloud the document which will now be placed before you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated. Now, Mr. Zhuniqi, we have before us the written transcript of the evidence you gave to the Tribunal before. And we also have your detailed statement so we know a great deal about the information you're able to give this trial. The purpose of you being here is so that counsel for the parties, for the Prosecution and for the accused, can ask you questions, either to add to the information you've already given, or to clarify it, or in some instances perhaps to challenge it. So it's important that we don't go back over the same evidence as you've already given, except in so far as it is necessary to make the position clear. We are anxious to get as much information as we can, and you can assist that process by concentrating your answers on the particular points that are raised in the questions. The first counsel to question you will be for the Prosecution, Ms. Moeller. Ms. Moeller.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Zhuniqi.

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Could you please state your name again for the record.

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: My name is Isuf Zhuniqi.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: And where are you from?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: From Orahovac municipality, Bellacerke village.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: And where did you live in March 1999?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: In the village, in Bellacerke.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Mr. Zhuniqi, did you give a statement to investigators of this Tribunal on 4 May 1999?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: And when you gave that statement, were photographs taken of some injuries that you had at the time?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: And on that occasion were you also taken to a clinic where an X-ray picture of your shoulder was made?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Did you then sign a declaration on the 31st May 2002 in which you declared that the statement that you gave in May 1999 was true and correct to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: When you came to the Tribunal this week, did you have the opportunity to read through your statement again?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: And do you declare today as well that this is the evidence you wish to give to this Court?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this point I would wish to tender Exhibit P331 [sic], which is the declaration and the statement; Exhibit P89, which are the photographs showing the injuries; and Exhibit P90 which is the X-ray photo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Oh, sorry, Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is highly technical, but I don't think the witness has told the Chamber that the contents of that statement are true and correct. The question was asked is this the evidence you wish to give to the Court. I'm not sure that that satisfies the requirement in that regard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, the rule that's -- I don't know if you have a copy of this rule, but it's a very recently introduced rule as a result of a change in rules a fortnight ago. And what it now requires is that the witness is present in court and attests that the written statement or the transcript, it applies both now to written statements and transcripts, accurately reflects that witness declaration and what the witness would say if examined. And I think that what Ms. Moeller has asked actually satisfies that test.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, I'm looking again, Your Honour, I think it doesn't. The question was: Do you declare today that this is the evidence you wish to give to the Court? That doesn't attest that it's accurate or anything else. It's just the evidence he wants to give you. That's very technical, I understand, but I'm not sure it meets the test.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, Ms. Moeller do you wants to dot the Is and cross the Ts?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can ask the witness differently, if that satisfies Mr. Ackerman and makes him happy, and if you think this is proper.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, the purpose here is not to make Mr. Ackerman happy, even though I enjoy being happy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah. Well, I think the wise course to follow here would be to remove any doubt, Ms. Moeller.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Yes. Certainly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Mr. Zhuniqi, you already confirmed that you read over your statement when you came here this week. Do you still declare today that what you said in the statement of May 1999 is true and correct to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Zhuniqi, did you also testify in the trial against Slobodan Milosevic in June 2002?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would like to tender the transcript of 6 June 2002 of the Milosevic trial, which is Exhibit P2332.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: And on this occasion I would like to point out that in the transcript the Exhibit number for the declaration and statement is not correct. It states it's 331 but the correct number is 2331.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just -- I've noted the statement now to have the number P331. Is that wrong?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: No, the correct number is 2331. It got lost in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Ah, right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Could we please call up Exhibit P93?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, before you do that, you have the same issue in relation to the transcript now, the way the rule is worded. That wasn't an issue before under the old rule.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. I will clarify this with the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Mr. Zhuniqi, your testimony in the trial against Slobodan Milosevic on 6 June 2002, is what you said then and there true and correct to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: Yes. It was true and correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Could we now please call up Exhibit 93? And it should be the seventh photo in this bundle. The Exhibit number should be 8872. So it's one further, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Mr. Zhuniqi, can you have a look at this photograph, please? Do you recognise this?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: What does it show?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: This is a photo of my village.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: In your statement, you mention that VJ tanks were entering your village on 25 March from Orahovac. Does this picture show the road on which these tanks were coming on?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Could the usher please assist the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Could you mark this road with an A, please. Could you draw an A on the screen?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: You want me to show you the direction where the tanks came from?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Yes. You basically have to write on the screen. You have to put an A where the street is.

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: [Marks]. The tanks came from Orahovac and stopped here at the mosque. My house is only 50 metres away from the mosque.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Okay. Just to clarify this, what you marked now is the mosque where the tanks arrived; correct? That's what you just said?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Okay. And could you see where your house was in relation to the mosque? Could you also mark that?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. My house is here.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Could we take a snapshot of this, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can you identify the second mark, what it is? We all know what's meant at the moment but later on, will we be clear?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Mr. Zhuniqi, the second mark you made, which is on the right-hand side of the mosque that you previously marked, is what again?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: I will tell you that the 12 tanks were stationed at the mosque because they were only 50 metres from my house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The mosque is the one on the left and the house is the one on the right. Is that correct, Mr. Zhuniqi?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, yes we can take that snapshot of that.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be IC53, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Could we now call up the first photo in the exhibit, Exhibit number 8866?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Mr. Zhuniqi, do you recognise this river and this bridge?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: Yes. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what the name of this stream is?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: This river and this bridge is called the river of Belaja, the bridge of Belaja.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: And is this the bridge and the stream that you refer to in your statement?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Can you mark again, and if the usher would assist, please, where you were hiding when the incident occurred?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: I was hiding under the bridge. About here.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Can you draft a letter A there, please.

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you also show the Court where the policemen were coming from and put a B at these locations, the letter B?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: The policemen were coming from here, on both sides of the stream.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Thank you. And can you now explain one thing about your testimony to the Judges? In your statement you say that you were in a group of about 700 villagers who were hiding in the stream. Now, we see on this picture that the bridge is relatively small. Where were all these people hiding?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: Behind this bridge, the people were there. This stream continues for kilometres, so we had -- we came here from the stream and when we stopped here on the bridge, the policemen came and stayed there. Part of them were on this side of the bridge and the other part was on that side of the bridge, and when they saw us on the right of the bridge, and -- they told us, "Just take off your clothes," and we were left in our underwear, and they kicked and punched us and took everything that they found in our clothes. And they told us, "Now put on your clothes and go to the other side of the stream."

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zhuniqi. Could you mark the two dots on the both sides of the river with a C, please.

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: And is it correct that you said that at this position the police came to this position?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Can we take a snapshot of this picture, please, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be IC54, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Mr. Zhuniqi, did you set out in your statement the names of all villagers that you saw being killed in the mass execution at the Belaja stream on this day?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: Yes. They all died. Would you like me to tell you the names?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: No, thank you. That's not necessary, Mr. Zhuniqi. The Chamber has your statement and can see all the names. I would just like to ask you --

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: Yes. They are in my statement and it is true that they all died.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: And when you came to the Tribunal this week, did you have an opportunity to look at a set of photographs of villagers from Bela Crkva?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: And did you look at each and every of these photos and say whether these were people who were killed in this incident?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: Yes. That's correct. All of them were killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is Exhibit 94, and due to the time-frame, we would like to tender it on the basis of this evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Mr. Zhuniqi, were you also shown a list of names this week and asked to go through the list of these names and say whether you recognised any of the persons listed therein as not having been killed on 25 March at the Belaja stream?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: All of them were killed on the 25th of March. All of them were killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Do you recall having gone through this list I'm referring to?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Can we call up Exhibit 97, please? The next page, please. Can we have the next page? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Mr. Zhuniqi, is that the list that we showed to you?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: And what do you say about this list? Is it a correct reflection of the people you saw being killed in the murder event on 25 March?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I saw this list, and it's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we are not tendering this list through this witness because it's part of a larger forensic report that we will tender through another witness. We just thought it would be beneficial to have a local person look through the names that was there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And how closely does it match Schedule B?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: It does match, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I'm sorry?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: It does match.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It does. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Zhuniqi, in your statement, and it is on page 3 of the English version, paragraph 2, you state that one of the policemen present there you knew from before. How did you know him?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: I worked -- I had a bus, and I knew that policeman very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: How did you know him? Where did you see him before this event?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: The -- at first, I had a small firm with buses, and I knew him very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Which route were you driving with your buses?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: The first time I saw him get on the bus, and he maltreated people, he asked for money, and that's where I knew him, where I saw him for the first time. I travelled from Gjakova to Prizren with my bus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: And you were driving the bus at that event when this person entered the bus?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, yes, the driver.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: And what would this person wear on this occasion? How was he dressed?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: The normal police uniform.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: What was the normal police uniform? What colour?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: The normal police uniform we call it yellow. I call it yellow.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Could you -- the colour that you just mention, do you see it in this courtroom? Could you point to this colour? Could you point to something that we could see as well?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: Well, yellow.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Is it this colour? And I'm --

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: No, no, it's not that colour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: If the record could reflect that I'm showing a yellow sticker.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, that's not what I consider yellow.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: So what would you say is the colour of the chairs on which the Judges sit, please?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: It's the upper part of the computer here. That's what I consider yellow.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: That's difficult to follow. Mr. Zhuniqi, could you say what is the colour of the chairs on which the Judges sit? Could you look at those?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: Yes. That colour. That's what I call yellow. But it was a little lighter.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: So the curtains' colour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Mr. Zhuniqi, did you find out later the name of this man that you saw in blue uniform when you were driving your bus and that you later saw at the stream in Bela Crkva?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, blue.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Sorry, I think there was a misunderstanding. Did you find out the name of the person we were talking about later?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: Yes. Nenad Matic.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Thank you. And you saw him in the group of the policemen who were at the Belaja stream shooting at the villagers?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Zhuniqi, in your statement, you say that you only found out when you were taken to the clinic when you gave your statement that you had a bullet lodged in your shoulder.

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Did you receive this bullet when the policemen shot at you at the Belaja stream?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Is this bullet today still in your shoulder?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, it is still in my shoulder.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zhuniqi.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: That would complete my questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Moeller. Mr. O'Sullivan, the order?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, General Ojdanic, General Pavkovic, Mr. Sainovic, Mr. Milutinovic, General Lukic and General Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll take the break now. Mr. Zhuniqi, we have to have a break now for half an hour, so if you could leave the courtroom you'll be shown where to go, and we'll see you again at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So the Court will resume in half an hour, at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Welcome back, Mr. Zhuniqi.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You will now be questioned by counsel representing the various accused. The first of these will be Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Zhuniqi. My name is Tomislav Visnjic and I represent General Ojdanic. I have a few questions for you, and on several occasions I will ask of you some clarifications of your previous statement. In your statement you stated that on the 25th of March, around 3.30, you were awakened by a loud noise coming from outside and then you saw 12 green tanks of the VJ came from the direction of Orahovac and stopped by the mosque. Later you gathered all the members of your immediate family and led them out of the house. Before I ask you any questions, I would kindly ask you to look at P93, page 10. It is a photograph, an aerial shot of your village. My first question is: How long did it take you to get from your house to the meadow to which you said you took your family members?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: When I saw 12 tanks and came out of my house, when I saw these 12 tanks by the mosque, it took me 15 minutes to leave my house because I could see the fire in the village. The village was on fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zhuniqi, on this photograph, can you indicate the spot where you and your family took refuge at around 3.30 or 4.00 on that day?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, so as not to have any confusion, this is an aerial shot taken from a different angle. Therefore, the witness's house is close to the mosque, somewhere within the triangle, but I hope the witness will get his bearings.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zhuniqi, can you see the mosque here? It should be around the centre of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us where you took your family?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: I my family -- well, at 50 metres from there is my house. I left the house, I saw the 12 tanks, and I went through here to the stream. You can see the stream here.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zhuniqi, can you indicate the spot where you and your family stayed for a while before going back to your house?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: When the tanks came, as I said, I left the house and through the houses in my neighbourhood I went to the stream, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We can't see what you're pointing out unless you actually draw it on to the screen, and I think you've marked so far the mosque and your house. Now, can you put another mark where you actually went to in the meadow?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I went to the meadow through here, through here, and I reached the Belaja stream.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zhuniqi, let us try to clarify this. In your statement of the 4th of May, 1999, you stated that you were awakened by the noise of the tanks and that you took your family out --

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: On the 4th of May --

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Just a moment, let me finish, please. You said that you took your family out of the house and that you hid in a place next to the village. Just a minute. It was in a field nearby, that there were about 200 people there and that after that, you again returned to your house. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: Please, I didn't understand the date you were referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Visnjic, the date is the 25th of March and not the 4th of May.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was not on the 4th of May, what you're describing.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour, I said that he gave the statement on the 4th of May. What took place there was on the 25th of March. That is not in dispute.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Can we agree on that, that the incident took place on the 25th of March?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Did you give your statement on the 4th of May, 1999?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Did you in that statement state that you left the house, and once the tanks left the village, you returned to your house again, subsequently?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: This is a different question. When the 12 tanks came, they passed through the village, they came at the outskirts of the village, and then returned again in the village. I went back to my house for 15 minutes only. After these 15 minutes, gunshots were coming from all sides of the village and then I went through the path that I marked and reached the stream.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Very well. My question was: Where did you go the first time you left the house?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: After the tanks returned, I went to the Belaja stream and to the railway bridge here.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: No, no. My question is: Once you left your house for the first time, as you mention in your statement, where did you go? To what field? Let us not get to the stream as yet. But once you left the house after having seen the tanks.

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: My house is here. I went here, and I took shelter there just while the tanks went to another village but they didn't go anywhere actually. They returned. So I went to this location here, stayed there for 15 minutes, and returned to my house. When I saw that the village was on fire, I fled again, here.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Can you mark the spot where you were and put the letter A there.

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Very well. You say that there was a column of tanks; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: I said I saw 12 tanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Were there any other vehicles that accompanied the tanks?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: No. I didn't see any other vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: In what direction did the tanks leave?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: In the direction of Celine village.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: When did you see the tanks return to your village?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: On the second time, I didn't see them go to any direction. I saw them going to the direction of Celine village the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: When did you see the tanks the second time?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: I didn't see the tanks the second time. I went to the stream. I was wounded there, and I could no longer see anything. I then went to Zuc village.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: After the tanks returned, how long did it take you to go back to your house? No, I apologise. I will rephrase. Once the tanks left, how long did it take you to go back to your house? Can you give us an estimate?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: It wasn't very far from my house. It took me 10, 15 minutes to get from that location back to my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: And at that moment, you didn't see any forces, be it the police or the military or any other unit in the village; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: No. At that moment, I didn't see anything, because I fled the village, as I said. I went outside the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Let us move on, then. Tell me this: As you were leaving the village the second time, across the field, as you marked it on the map and en route to the bridge, none of your family members, or anyone else for that matter, was hit from a firearm in that interval of time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: I was the only one from my immediate family to be hit by a firearm. And as for more distant relatives, 18 of my distant cousins were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zhuniqi, as of the moment when you left your house and up until you reached the bridge where you hid, during that time, do you know whether anyone was wounded?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: But you said there was firing?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: Yes. There was firing.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Having reached the bridge, I just wanted to clarify what seems to be a discrepancy in your statement, in the Milosevic transcript, on page 6451, you said you were not under the bridge but, rather, in an irrigation channel. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: That is correct. The irrigation canal is annexed to the stream.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: So you were not hiding under the bridge, as you indicated on this photograph today, but rather, you were in an irrigation canal. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: You can see it very well here that next to the bridge is the canal.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, before we show the next photograph, could we assign a number, an IC number, to this photograph?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Before we do that, Mr. Visnjic, I'm not clear on the mark at the top of the photograph. Is that supposed to be the bridge?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I understood the witness -- well, I can ask him again.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zhuniqi, the last red dot you marked on this photograph, is this where the bridge over the Belaja stream is?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: Yes. The first dot is on this side of the bridge, and the second is on the other side of the bridge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. So we can take a --

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honour, for the transcript, these are the two dots on the photograph towards the upper part of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So we can take a snapshot now of this.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be IC55, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: I may have missed something, but as regards this exhibit, could we again please have page 2, this being a set of photographs. So page -- Mr. Zhuniqi, can you see the irrigation canal on this photograph, the one you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: Yes. You can see it very well. It is below the bridge, this irrigation canal. This is a canal.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Can you mark the spot where you hid on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is there some significance in the exact place at which one of 700 people actually was? I'd like to know if there is a real -- if there's an important issue here that we can focus our minds on. Bearing in mind I think he said there were 700 people there.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree, but my next question is what I was trying to get to with this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Were there any caves used as shelters close to this bridge, Mr. Zhuniqi?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the basis for this question is 3D122, page 0075530, which is a statement of another person.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zhuniqi --

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we give this photograph a number and then I can move on.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be IC56, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zhuniqi, did you know that the KLA arrived at Bela Crvka and armed the villagers so that the villagers could defend the village against the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: There was no KLA at Bellacerke and they did not arm the villagers.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zhuniqi, did you know that there was civilian protection in the village which in true fact represented an armed unit of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: No. That's not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zhuniqi, did you know that members of the civilian protection left their houses armed and they took the same direction towards the bridge and the Belaja stream just prior to the arrival of the Serbian forces?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: No. Nobody was armed. We were farmers, women, children. All of them who left the houses and went to the stream were civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: And you didn't see anyone carrying a weapon among the group of people who were hiding close to the bridge?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: I didn't see a single person with a weapon. Nobody had a weapon. And I'm completely aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Do you know Popaj Nesret, Mr. Zhuniqi?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: I know him as a villager, as a co-villager.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Just to steer clear of any confusion, was he born around 1963? Therefore, he could be around 40 years of age today?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know his age. There are many Nesrets. I know one of them, but it was of no interest to me to know his birth date.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: The Nesret you know, is his first name Popaj?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Is his last name Popaj?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Did you know, Mr. Zhuniqi, that Popaj Nesret stated that he was a member of the civilian protection and that armed with a rifle he also headed towards the Belaja stream on the same day at the same time, when you and the other people headed the same way?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: That is not true. I didn't see Nesret and I didn't see him carrying any weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zhuniqi, did you know that at this locality, close to the river between Bela Crkva and Xerxe some KLA members were seen as early as the 1st of March, 1999?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: I told you earlier that in Bellacerke I did not see any KLA, and there was no KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: And was there any KLA presence in Celine?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: I did not see any in the Celine village. I was wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: And do you know that before you were wounded, members of the KLA held positions near the village of Celine on the 25th of March, 1999?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: I told you that I did not see any in Celine.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Did you hear about that?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Zhuniqi, you said in your statement that before the attack started, nothing meaningful was going on in your village. Now I would like to ask you about the following. Do you know that on the 21st of January, 1999, in an ambush near Bela Crvka, a KLA fighter was killed and that his funeral in the village of Labucevo was attended by about 2.000 civilians and 700 KLA fighters?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: I don't remember this. I don't know anything about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Since this is a large number of people, Mr. Zhuniqi, didn't some of these people take your bus to attend the funeral?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: My bus did the route Gjakova-Prizren, and I was not interested in those matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What was the name of the -- Mr. Visnjic, what was the name of the village where the funeral was.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Labucevo. Labucevo. 3D114.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Zhuniqi, how far is Labucevo from Bellacerke?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Over 30 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zhuniqi, do you know that on the 27th of February, 1999, a Serb was abducted near the village of Velika Krusa after which there was an exchange of gunfire between the KLA and the Serbs, due to which 400 to 600 people fled to Bela Crkva to stay with their relatives?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: I don't know about this. I haven't heard about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zhuniqi, were you in the village during that period or, rather, at that time, on the 27th of February, 1999?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: I can't remember. I was driving the bus. I was paying attention to my business. I did not pay attention to those matters. Other people did maybe, but I had my own business.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: All right. Is it correct, Mr. Zhuniqi, that on the 18th or the 19th of March the police took up a strategic position at a place called Brdo near Bela Crkva?

utterances.speaker: ISUF ZHUNIQI
utterances.text: Yes. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
