As I said, the village -- the population was in the village and the main road was running through the village. So what would have happened if NATO bombed there? It would have been a massacre.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yeah, that could have been pretty bad, couldn't it? These forces that you describe, these Serb forces that were moving along this road that goes through your village, they were the forces of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: Yes. Of what remained from Yugoslavia, because at that time Yugoslavia did not exist as such an entity.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Kosovo was part of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, still is -- well, not now, it's part of Serbia. But it was at that time part of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: It used to be but whether it is still, that is for someone else to decide. I cannot answer this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I'm talking about March of 1999. It was then, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: Yes. But in your question you said that it still is. I'm not competent to answer that question because someone else decides on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I don't even need you to answer that question. It's not important. I think you'll concede and agree with me that if there were Serb forces present in your village like you say, on that date and moving along a road through your village, they had every right to be there because they were in the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and they were forces of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. They weren't invading anybody. That was where they belonged, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: They would pass through on other occasions as well, but this time it was different and with a different purpose.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, they had every right to try to defend that part of the Republic of Serbia, Republic of Yugoslavia, from terrorists and from NATO attacks, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: NATO was not on the ground. It wasn't in our village. And at that time, there were no terrorist groups in our village. This was just a revenge over the population because of the NATO bombings.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, I know that that's your position and you have every right to take that position, if you wish. In the village of Krusha e Madhe, there was a Serb family, the head of which was a guy named Boski. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And on the 25th of March, 1999, in that village, Boski led a gang of hooligans who started burning and looting the houses in your village, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And this Boski even started wearing a green camouflage uniform, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: They were all wearing that kind of uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I asked you about Boski. Boski was wearing a green camouflage uniform, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: Including Boski, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And Boski wasn't a member of the army of Yugoslavia, was he? He was a civilian wearing a green camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: You left your village that day and took refuge in a valley that you -- that was between a couple of hills where you could make observations.

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I'm wondering if you left before or after Boski started his burning and looting in your village.

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: This has been explained in my statement. We were above Krusha e Madhe village. We spent the night in the valley. From the hill above Krusha e Madhe, you can see the village very well. And as for the night, as I said, we spent it in the valley.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I wonder if you could answer the question now, Dr. Hoti, which was whether you left before or after Boski started his burning and looting? In other words, did you move out of the village before or after he started the burning and looting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We went to the valley after the burning occurred. We observed from the hill above the village. When it became dark, we went to the valley because we felt safer there. So it was after Boski's activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: So you had no problem observing Boski's activities and identifying him as the person leading this group, did you?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Now, I want to go now to the 26th of March, the next day --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just before you do that, please, Mr. Ackerman. Dr. Hoti, I had the impression that you had left the village much earlier in the day. At what time did you actually leave the village itself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the morning. And I explained in my statement as well that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Please bear in mind I don't have your statement. I've relying on what you've told us here today, all right? So we are trying to get answers to questions that we have in our minds. We don't necessarily have the same thought -- all have the same thoughts. So I would like to know what time --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- you took your family to the hill above the village.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Immediately after the encirclement, after we saw the forces coming. We immediately went above the village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: By that time, had Boski started burning and looting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Later, not exactly at the time when we left, but sometime in the afternoon, a couple of hours later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The evidence is now completely different from what it was a moment ago because you weren't answering the question you were asked earlier. Please listen carefully to the question, and I assure you it's an important answer. Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: So your observation of what Boski was doing was made from outside the village?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: How many people were in this gang that Boski was leading?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: A few. I didn't count them. It was a group.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Can you make any kind of an estimate? Was it hundreds or was it tens?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: Tens.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: All right. Now I want to go to the 26th of March -- I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt again, but just to be clear --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: No problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: When you were observing from the hill, were there any tanks still visible to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The tanks were stationed there. They no longer moved.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: On the 26th of March, you talk about joining up with a group of people from Hoca e Vogel who told you they had been told to go to Albania. And so you started walking, you said in the direction of Krusha e Madhe, right?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: So you're walking back toward the town that you had already left?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: There was no other road. We did not go back to Krusa proper because we were stopped.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: There was a point where you were stopped, I know, by the police and you were told to go to -- in the direction of Nagavc, right?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Now, some of these people who had stopped you at that point were recognised by some of the people who were with you as former neighbours, persons they had lived next to?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: I was saying this with reference to another event.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, so that was not the case when you were walking toward Nagavc; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Okay. What was the condition of the -- yes, you are right, because it was when you arrived in Nagavc that some uniformed people came and started collecting money from you; correct?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: These were the people that were recognised, some of them were recognised as former neighbours of people that were with you?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: What was the condition of the village of Nagavc when you first arrived there?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: There were some houses that were burned and destroyed but the majority of houses were not.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And were there -- were there soldiers around the village of Nagavc, in the area around that village?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: We didn't see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: So the only forces that you saw of any kind were those that came in the village and were demanding money from you?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And did they remain there or did they leave?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: They left in an unknown direction. I didn't know where they went to but they left.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: It's difficult to figure out the time-frame. However, in the Milosevic transcript, at page 3614, you said, in a response to a question from Mr. Milosevic: "The Serbian forces were always on the hills round about us." Was that -- was that true with regard to the time you were in Nagavc?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: These were the words of the soldier. He took me and took my money. He said to me, "We are around in the hills and we are observing and watching you, every movement, so don't leave your houses." These were his words.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: All right. The last thing I want to talk to you about is this bombing incident that you described in Nagavc. This happened at 2.00 in the morning in the dark. I take it you would agree that it would have been impossible to actually see and identify the aircraft that was involved in this?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: I said earlier that it was not possible to see the aircraft.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And you talked about the sound that this aircraft made compared to the NATO airplanes that you'd been hearing every day and it was different because it was flying very low. So it had a different sound to it; correct?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: Yes. It was a different noise because it was flying low. While during the nine days, when the NATO bombing occurred, the noise was not that strong. This is the difference.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And so you concluded because this particular aircraft was flying low and made a different sound, that it was not a NATO aircraft but a Serbian aircraft. Is that -- is that the basis of your conclusion?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: What aircraft that was, whom it belonged to, it is up to the military people to decide. They can see the pieces of bombs here and there and they can analyse them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Do you know anything about cruise missiles and that they fly at very low altitudes?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: I have never heard or read about those missiles.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: All right. I think it's probably true, and it's probably the case, that your position on this is pretty much exactly what you told Mr. Milosevic on page 3610 at line 8, when you said: "I can't say whether it was your aircraft or NATO's. All I can mention here is what I have heard and seen." And that's really your evidence and your testimony, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Sir, thank you for your attention. I don't have any more questions of you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman, is that transcript an exhibit? Or does it have an exhibit number?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: It is, Your Honour. I think it's 4D24 -- 4D25.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Good day, Dr. Hoti. My name is Dan Ivetic, and I'm one of the attorneys representing Mr. Sreten Lukic in this trial and I'm assisted by Branko Lukic and Ozren Ogrizovic, and I'm going to ask you a few questions to clarify and better understand your testimony, so please bear with me. Now, my first question has to do with your home village of Velika Krusa, or Krusha e Madhe in the Albanian. Now, first of all, in the Milosevic proceedings, you stated that the KLA -- that the KLA did not have a presence in your village. Is it still your testimony today that the KLA was not present in Velika Krusa or Krusha e Madhe?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: Yes, it is. I say it with full responsibility that the KLA did not operate at that time there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. You say at that time. Let me ask you some specific questions. In -- in March of 1999, isn't it true that there were armed KLA fighters in and around your village of Velika Krusa, both in uniform and in civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: No, that's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Was there a KLA presence in your village, in either 1998 or 1999, at any time?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: The KLA was not in Krusha e Madhe. It had never been, because the village is very close to the main road, and the forces, the Serb forces, the army and so on, moved along that road. So there was no KLA presence in Krusha e Madhe, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with an individual named Ragip or Ragip Hoti from Krusha e Madhe?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: Yes. I know him. He's a cousin of mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And isn't it true that Ragip Hoti was the commander of the KLA forces, the KLA detachment, that was located in Krusha e Madhe village in 1998 and 1999?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: Ragip Hoti was a soldier. He was not a commander. I don't know about that. But he was not operating in Krusha e Madhe. He was with the KLA where the KLA was operating.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Well, where is it that the KLA was operating, if they were not operating in Krusha e Madhe?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: In the inner villages, Semetisht, Samadrexha, Drenoc, in the Malisheve area but not in Krusha e Madhe.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: How many kilometres were these areas from Krusha e Madhe?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: The closest village is over 20 kilometres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: All right. So if we could focus, then, on the critical dates in March, that is around the 25th and 26th of March, 1999, when you say that these forces surrounded the village of Krusha e Madhe and when people began to leave Krusha e Madhe. I'd like to ask you if, in fact, any individuals that were KLA fighters were present in Krusha e Madhe during that critical point in time?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: I said it earlier. I'm repeating it again. There was no presence, no KLA presence, in the Krusha e Madhe.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: All right. Well, let me ask you about a couple more specific individuals. Do you know someone named Naser Krasniqi, aged 22, or at least he was aged 22 in 1999, from Krusha e Madhe who was a member of the KLA? Was he there on March the 25th or March the 26th, 1999?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: Naser Krasniqi is not from Krusha e Madhe, and he was not there in Krusha e Madhe. He was in those places where the KLA was. There was no soldier, no KLA soldier, in uniform there in Krusha e Madhe that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Are you familiar with an individual named Enver Hoti, born in 1970 in Krusha e Madhe, the son of Jahir Hoti?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: Yes. Enver Hoti was never a soldier of the KLA. He still lives in Krusha e Madhe today. He was never a member of the KLA. I think you've got the wrong information. I know him very well. He's a relative of mine. He never was a KLA member.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You state that you know him very well and that he's a relative of yours. Was he there on the -- on this critical date when people began to leave Krusha e Madhe?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did he leave with the group that you were with from Krusha e Madhe on that day?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this time I would ask for Exhibit 6 D80 to be put up on e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And sir, while we are waiting for that, do you know whether, in fact, Enver Hoti gave a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor of the Tribunal, a sworn statement?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if I could first direct your attention, and I have to apologise, sir, I only have this document in English because that is how it was given to me by the Office of the Prosecutor so I will have to read portions of it for it to be translated to you. So please bear with me. If I can direct your attention to the second page of that exhibit, we are looking at the first page now, and if we could zoom in on the top portion, this witness statement begins, sir, with the words: "I was born in Krusha e Madhe and lived there all my life" -- all my live, actually. "I am married with Shpresa, 27 years old, and have three children, Erkan, 8 years old; Erenita, five years old; and Erlanda, three years old. I lived together with my parents, Hoti, Jahir, 56 years old, and Hazize, 50 years old, and an aunt, Hoti, Naxhie." And I apologise for the translations -- for the pronunciations. Sir, is this the Enver Hoti that you had known very well who is a relative of yours and who left Krusha e Madhe with you?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: Yes, this is the one.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. If I could have --

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: Yes, it's him.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now if I can have the document scrolled down to the excerpt dealing with the date in question, and again I'm going to have to read this for you so you can get the translation, sir. According to Enver's words, he says, and I quote: "I had seen the tanks before patrolling the same road but this time there was much more than I had seen before. After we had seen all these tanks. All the young men gathered in the village. An UCK soldier spoke with us and told us that nothing should happen to us, that the Serbs were just passing by. Everyone went home." Now, Dr. Hoti, do the words of your relative Enver Hoti refresh your recollection as to whether or not there were KLA fighters present in your village of Krusha e Madhe?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: Earlier you told me that Enver Hoti was a soldier in the KLA. You can see from this document that Enver Hoti was not a soldier but he was a simple villager. He said these words and he's responsible for those words. And I told you earlier that I never saw a KLA soldier that day. I did not see this soldier. You can ask him. He can give you an answer about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: All right. If I can now direct your attention to the next page of this exhibit, and -- strike that. I need to start at the bottom of the last page. It flows over the pages so we are going to have to start at the bottom of the last sentence and flow on to the next page where Enver Hoti describes how he left his home. The previous page. It's page 3, page 2 in e-court, the bottom. And beginning with the last sentence: "There were not so many people in the village anymore because the most had" -- and then we had to go to the next page in e-court. "Most had left at about 0400 hours which we did not know. I left the house and saw Krasniqi, Naser, about 22 years old, and Krasniqi, Selim, about 31 years old, at the centre of the village and talked to them. I asked them what was going on, and they told me to leave because the village was surrounded. They were wearing civilian clothes but carrying automatic rifles. I had seen Naser before in an UCK uniform. At that moment, I did not hear any shelling or shooting. All the young men had left." And then he talks about another friend that he met in the hill where the mosque from Krusha e Madhe was. He says: "I met a friend of mine there. He was carrying an automatic rifle, and I asked him where to go. He said that I should go wherever I could go. That friend worked as a mechanic for the UCK but he was not wearing a uniform." Now, Dr. Hoti, do these words of your relative refresh your recollection of whether there were armed UCK fighters in civilian clothes present in your village directing people where to go precisely upon the critical date in March when people began leaving the village?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: First of all, it is not up to me to comment on the statement of a person who is alive. And secondly, I can tell you that I never saw any of these mentioned here, but if this person saw them, he can testify. But I will tell you this: Of the 206 people from Krusa who were killed that day, all of them were civilians. There were no soldiers there. No soldiers were killed at that day. So all of them were civilians. So you can ask that gentleman about his statement. I am not responsible for his statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, sir, you did identify that this individual Enver Hoti left Krusha e Madhe with you and so I'm just trying to find out why the description of who was in the village and who wasn't in the village is so different. Now, as a final question relating to this document, I'd like to have the last page put up on e-court just so that there is no confusion about the identity of this individual, because apparently when he gave his statement in Albania, this was attached to it, and I would ask you whether in fact the picture on this identification document is of Enver Hoti.

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: I can't see it very clearly, the photograph, I mean, but the name is there. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And is this in fact a Yugoslavian driving ID or permit?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I have to ask you about the activities of the KLA combatants. Did you ever as a medical doctor treat KLA combatants for wounds they received in either 1998 or 1999?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: I treated soldiers in my clinic when they came there but I also treated civilian -- the civilian population, because as a doctor I did not make any distinction. Whether they were soldiers or civilians or whatever nationality they were, I treated all.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And when you say that you treated soldiers, are we talking about KLA soldiers or some other type of soldier?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: No. No other organisation. They did not come in KLA uniform. I thought they were from the KLA but when they came to my clinic, they were in civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So -- and, first of all, your clinic is located in Krusha e Madhe; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So is it your understanding that when the KLA fighters would come to Krusha e Madhe, they would not wear their uniforms but would wear civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, you stated that there were a number of people from Opterusha present in your village as a result of the 1998 offensives that were directed against the KLA that were in that village. I want to ask you if you are aware of any actions undertaken by the KLA to kidnap civilians from any village, such as Opterusha, in the municipality of Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: No. I'm not aware.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Would you be surprised, then, to find out that on the 16th of July, 1998, the UCK kidnapped every single Serb civilian from the village of Opterusha?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: I don't know about this either.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did the many civilians that you said came from Opterusha to Krusha e Madhe not discuss such a large scale action by the KLA in the village that they had come from?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: I said that something happened there, that there was fighting. That's why they moved out of that village. They did not live in that village anymore. But I don't know anyone, neither Albanian or -- either Albanian or Serb.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not catch the last part of the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, they need you to complete your answer. The translation stopped after you said "neither Albanian or Serb." Actually, I strike that. It stopped after you said "either Albanian or Serb." Could you please repeat your answer so that we can have it?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: From the village of Opterusha. I did not know anyone from Opterusha because it was far away from my village.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now I'd like to move ahead to the time-period that you were in Nogavac and you talked about this individual in a multi-coloured uniform whose colour you could not remember, who had a moustache and a dark complexion, whose friends had bandanas and red, white and blue paint on their face. I understand you could not identify the colour of the uniform but did you see any tags on the uniform?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: No. Because in those moments, it's difficult to see those things, when you have a gun pointed at you. It's difficult. You cannot see those signs or tags.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: One moment, Your Honour. I need to consult with my colleague and see what other areas I -- if I missed any.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I'm done.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Dr. Hoti for your testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. O'Sullivan.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: No questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac?.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, all I have left is one question. And by your leave I wanted to ask Dr. Hoti the following.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Dr. Hoti, is it correct that on the 25th of September, two days ago, that is, you spoke with the Office of the Prosecutor and that you provided some additional information?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Is it correct that these two days ago, when you spoke with the OTP, you said that soldiers of the army of Yugoslavia usually behaved in a fair way towards the refugees?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: Yes. The soldiers behaved better, always behaved better.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Dr. Hoti.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: No questions, Your Honour. I'm sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I'll take the first answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hoti, I have a few questions concerning the period immediately prior to the outbreak of the conflict regarding the events which took place in your village of Velika Krusa and its environs. Did you know that on the 27th of February, 1999, a Serb was abducted from the vicinity of the village of Velika Krusa after which an exchange of fire ensued between the KLA and the Serbs, the consequence of which were 400 to 600 people who fled to Bela --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't catch the last toponym.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: To the village of Bela Crkva?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: I would like to know which village. When you say a village close to Krusha e Madhe, which village do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Did you know that on the 27th of February, 1999, close to your village of Velika Krusa, a Serb was kidnapped by the KLA after which there was an exchange of fire between the KLA and the Serb forces?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: Yes, but I'm asking you again which village do you mean? Where was this fighting taking place? Because if you say close to Krusha e Madhe, I don't know what you mean. I have to know the name of the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let me put it this way. On the 27th of February, were there 400 to 600 inhabitants of Velika Krusa who fled to Bela Crkva to their relatives?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: No. That's not correct. Nobody moved from Velika Krusa at that time. It was calm.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have 3D113 shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hoti I wanted to read out a part of this exhibit, this being a report. I believe we'll have to wait for it to be put on the screen. Mr. Hoti, this is a report by the European Monitoring Mission dated the 27th of February, in which they describe events which took place in the vicinity of your village. In paragraph 1 of the report, it reads the following: "[In English] At 1530 hours on 27 February, a Serb was abducted in the vicinity of Randobrava, three kilometres east of Velika Krusa." [Interpretation] Then: "[In English] At 1900 hours outside Velika Krusa, machine-gun fire and one mortar shell was fired, likely by Serbs. "People in Velika Krusa panicked, and some 400 to 600 fled to Bela Crkva. Most of them could find shelter with relatives. The team met around 100 IDPs on tractor and horse coaches, all heading towards Bela Crkva." [Interpretation] Refugees. Mr. Hoti, are you aware of this incident?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: First of all, the village of Randobrava had never Serbs living there. Now, the question is how come this Serb was there and abducted? Secondly, it's not clear to me how these people fled to Bela Crkva.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's not the question. The question is whether you're aware of 400 to 600 people fleeing from your village to Bela Crkva.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's the only question that's being asked at the moment. And your answer to that is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I have never heard of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know a person by the name of Sebahudin Cena from Velika Krusa, who was otherwise a KLA commander in the special police?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: Many things are mixed up here. Sebahudin Cena is from Orahovac, he's alive. He works and lives there. He's not from Krusha e Madhe. He worked and lived in Orahovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: All right. And did you hear that in the village of Celine which is near you on the 5th of March, 1999, 12 members of the KLA, of the special police of the KLA, broke into the yard of Gezim Rexhepi, among them was this Sebahudin Cena as well, and they tried to kill a person, and they abducted another person? Have you heard of that incident?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: This person you mention, was it a Serb or Albanian, because there is no Serb in Celine. All of them there are Albanians.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: That person's name is Hazim Terjeni, the person who was abducted.

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: There is no person by last name Terjeni in Celine.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: So you never heard even of a similar incident?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: No. I didn't hear because, as I said, there is no Terjeni family in Celine.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: All right. Could you please tell me the following? Do you know Ilir Hoti and Nexhmedin Hoti from Velika Krusa?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: There are several Ilirs. If that's the one I think, I know him. I don't know which Ilir in particular you are referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: I'm giving you the following names now. Ilir Hoti and Nexhmedin Hoti, both of them members of the KLA, from Velika Krusa.

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: Ilir Hoti during this time worked and lived in Switzerland. He still works and lives there. As for Nexhmedin Hoti, he was a disabled person, and I don't think a disabled person can be a member of the KLA. Nexhmedin was killed but by your forces. So, as, said, I don't believe that a disabled person could be a member of the KLA. As for Ilir he was never in Kosovo at that time. He was in Switzerland.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Then obviously there is a person by the name of Sejfullah Hoti who made our -- an erroneous statement to the OTP of this Tribunal but then let's move on. Do you know the name of Rashkaj Petrit from your village, Velika Krusa?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: This person, too, is not from Krusha e Madhe. He is from Krusha e Vogel. These are two different villages, not one village.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I hate to interrupt Mr. Visnjic at that point. I'm just noting that the transcript is void of most of the correct names. Can we trust that the names will be filled in? It may play a role later in the case that we have the correct names in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, that's normally what happens, is the transcript is updated. So I don't think there is any reason to think it will be any different today.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: If there is a problem tomorrow when you see the transcript, you can raise it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: I will. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, let me just help my colleague, the page is ERN 0076-5392. That is where she will find the exact name.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: So you are right, Mr. Hoti, Rashkaj Petrit is indeed from Mala Krusa but he stated the following. "There were members of the KLA in the village of Mala Krusa but at the moment when we were taken prisoner, there weren't any. There were a few of their bases in Velika Krusa but not in our village." Mr. Hoti, is Mr. Rashkaj Petrit right?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: I never ever mentioned the village of Krusha e Vogel. I never circled it on the map. As for Krusha e Vogel, there are witnesses who can testify about that particular village. I am here to testify about Krusha e Madhe, which is a different village.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Maybe we haven't understood each other. Witness Rashkaj said there were a few bases of the KLA in Velika Krusa. That is his assertion. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: I cannot confirm or deny somebody else's words. What I said from the very beginning, and I repeat it now, there was no KLA presence.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Excuse me again, Your Honour, but could the name witness be filled in? What was the name, please? Could that be clarified?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I don't know it's not being done. Could you give that name again, please, Mr. Visnjic?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Petrit Rashkaj. And again the same page, the same ERN number that I gave a few minutes ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hoti, is this the right information, that in your village, there is a certain pizzeria that is owned by Gazmend Malesori?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: Are you talking about then or now? Can you clarify that, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Whenever I put questions to you I'm referring to 1999. So is Gazmend Malesori a person from your village? Let's start that way.

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Right. Does he own a pizzeria?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: I said yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Hamza and Halim Bellanica, are they from your village?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Now I'm going to read out to you a portion of 3D98, which reads as follows. It's also part of a witness statement and it says the following: "The witness stayed in the village and Hamza and Halim Bellanica were members of the KLA. Halim was armed with an AK 47 rifle and he went to his KLA base in the village which was in the pizzeria of Gazmend Malesori."

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I object to the use of this document. According to what we received, 3D98 is not a witness statement, but it is a document that is not specified in terms of its source or anything that is titled KLA presence, DEM 2. And it seems to be a collection of some sort.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right, Your Honour. It is a collection that was provided to us by the OTP. Right at this moment I cannot give you the exact date, but it was on a CD that was submitted to us in 2003. We are looking for the relevant information right now. I can provide it immediately after this hearing. I can give the date of disclosure by the OTP and what --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The objection is that you've characterised it as part of a witness statement. Now, is it a witness statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps we can actually have it displayed. It is 3D98, page 55. 3D98, page 55. I've just been told now that this material was disclosed to us by the OTP on the 23rd of October, 2002.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes. But what is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is material that contains [In English] -- of KLA in Kosovo. These 8 spreadsheets were prepared by the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I can't see on it who it's referring to, though, at any stage. These -- these are anonymous, are they? You're just going to put some anonymous information; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, what I'm putting to the witness is what I received from the OTP. I received it as anonymous information. If they are challenging that now, and it's their very own document, then I think that we've entered a new stage. I will withdraw my question but I would really like to hear them first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It's not their document, Mr. Visnjic. This is a material which they have which they've disclosed to you, as I understand it. Now, before we can make use of it, meaningful use of it, we need to know what it is, and at the moment I'm floundering in my attempt to identify what it is. For example, the bit on the screen doesn't have any names on it. Now, is it because part of the page is missing or what?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, what we got from the OTP is documentation that is contained in eight -- in eight special entities that are defined as KLA presence [In English] KLA incidents, KLA activity, KLA killings of non-Albanians, KLA missing non-Albanians.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And is it one of the passages on the screen that you were putting to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But I think it's not on this page. Then I really have a problem if I gave that page reference. Just a moment, please. I see. My colleague is telling me that it is page 57 on the screen. Can we see the next one? We are looking -- sorry, 55.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, thank you. Now, Ms. Moeller what exactly is the objection?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: The objection is, Your Honour, is that first of all Mr. Visnjic referred to that being a witness statement to -- to -- confronting the witness with it. It's not clear who is that witness and also it's just one page excerpt from a document that is -- who -- which purpose is unclear at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. I will repel that objection because all that is happening here is that Mr. Visnjic is putting a question which is based on information he has in his possession which came from the Office of the Prosecution and therefore that's an adequate foundation for the question. I'll then ask the question myself to try to speed this process up. I think the question that Mr. Visnjic wants to ask you is whether the names Hamza and Halim Bellanica are familiar to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Hamza and Halim Bellanica are from Krusha e Madhe and they live in Krusha e Madhe even today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is it correct that they were KLA members?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. They were not KLA members. I've never seen them with --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You've never seen them with what, sorry?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In KLA clothes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Have you ever seen either of them carrying a weapon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. He could have had that weapon that day, but personally I didn't see him with a weapon and I didn't hear that he used that weapon. The person who had seen him with a weapon should be held responsible for his words.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And what do you make of the proposition that there was a KLA base in your village located at Gazmend Malesori's pizzeria?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That term itself, "pizzeria," "restaurant," was used maybe every now and then by a KLA soldiers for them to eat lunch because it is normal for someone to go to a restaurant to eat or drink something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]. .

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hoti, Behra Dalip, does that name sound familiar to you?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: Dalip Behra, yes. He was killed. He was a KLA member, but he was not killed in Krusa. He was killed at a location where fightings against the KLA was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: I just asked you whether the name was familiar to you.

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: Yes, it is familiar to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Right. What about Arben Behra, also from your village? Was he a member of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: Yes. Don't know about him.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have no further questions of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Ms. Moeller.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I also object to the admission of Exhibit 6 D80, the statement of Enver Hoti in the current format as provided by the Defence. The basis for this objection is that my learned friend Mr. Ivetic addressed twice with Dr. Hoti the question that Enver Hoti fled together with Dr. Hoti, and by this I think the part of the statement that address the flight of Enver Hoti became part of the cross-examination and should be included in the statement that is submitted as well. That would be page 1 and 2 of the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You mean that's part of the statement not referred to?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: That's part of the statement that Mr. Ivetic referred to by asking whether Enver Hoti fled together with Dr. -- with Dr. Hoti and it was cut out of the version of the statement that is submitted by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, that's --

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: We submit the parts that are submitted are taken out of context.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Ivetic, what's being proposed is that you should have the whole statement presented.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If I recall correctly, we have been at this several times and we've decided that excerpts from transcripts that have been discussed in cross-examination will come in rather than the whole transcript. We had the same situation with another statement that I used the other day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's correct in so far as you can isolate that particular element or passage, but what's being suggested here is that you need to see the context to put the evidence in its proper context.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If you look at the section that I quoted, the context, i.e., the parts around it that I didn't quote are actually in the exhibit. The witness is the one that stated for the first time that he -- that Enver Hoti left with him. I cross-examined him about -- specifically upon his recollection of whether there were KLA members present and that is what is submitted in my exhibit. I don't know what the Prosecution wants. If they want me to be presenting their witness statements in toto in my case, it sounds like they want me to do their job for them. I presented what is relevant to my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You have a reason for opposing this, have you?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yeah, on principle. I think that it's improper. If they want to present evidence, they should present it. And I confronted the witness with portions of the statement, the sworn statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, "confrontation" is not the appropriate word here because it's not his statement. What you're doing is you're putting questions which are based on someone else's statement, and there is nothing wrong with that. You're putting parts on the screen to clarify that. But I don't think it's confrontation. What's being said against that is that because it's someone else's statement you need to see more of the context to understand properly the evidence that's given in response by this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: But I believe the role that we have been having in this trial is that only parts that are referenced in testimony are -- become part of the evidence, so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, they don't even necessarily become part of the evidence. They are on the record because they were used and they help an understanding of the evidence that's actually given by the witnesses. But here it's being suggested that to do that job properly you need to see more of the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: But, Your Honour, if you look at the exhibit, it references the day, it references the village, and it references what he saw. What other context would be necessary to having that understanding, I don't know, because the witness -- this witness testified that there was never a KLA presence in the village before I used the exhibit to try and refresh his recollection. So I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Give me, please, Ms. Moeller, an example of what you think from this statement would help us to understand the evidence better.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Well, the issue here is, Your Honours, that by asking Dr. Hoti twice whether Enver Hoti fled with him, Mr. Ivetic gave the suggestion to the Court that the two of them were actually together all the time and that Dr. Hoti, by saying that he did not see any KLA soldier and he did not see the persons that Enver Hoti referred to in his statement, he may not have been truthful. Now, if you look at the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, I specifically noted that this witness -- it doesn't follow for a moment that this witness was with Enver Hoti the whole time. I specifically made that note as the evidence went along. It's clear from his evidence that he did not say he was in his company all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I might add the exhibit itself also doesn't mention that he was with him at that time, so ...

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Very well. Because that was not clear on the record for me. And if you look at the parts of the statement of Enver Hoti that were cut out, it becomes very clear how this witness fled.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But we are not having regard to the evidence of Enver Hoti. It's not before us as his evidence. It's before us as the basis for a question. The issue for us will be how much of what is put to him this witness accepts or denies. But Enver Hoti's statement isn't a piece of the evidence that we are considering as a separate piece of evidence in the case.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, certainly not. But I understood that this witness confirmed twice that he and Enver Hoti were fleeing together.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, you can ask him now in re-examination to clarify the position if you're in any doubt. But it doesn't require any more of the statement admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Very well. That's the alternative approach I wish to take to clarify this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, well, please do that then.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOELLER
utterances.text: Dr. Hoti, how many people fled out of your village that day, out of Krusha e Madhe that day?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: To where? To Albania?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOELLER
utterances.text: When you first fled your village on the 25th of March.

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: I said earlier that we left in two directions; one towards Nagavc and the other above Krusa. So not everybody went in the same direction but the whole village left but in two directions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOELLER
utterances.text: And how many people would there have been, the whole village?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: Well, I said there were 6.000 inhabitants in the village, but there were other people who came, so there were 3.000 or 4.000. But they left in two directions, all of this -- all of those people.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOELLER
utterances.text: And did you flee on foot or on a tractor or in a car?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: Some on tractors or in cars. Me, personally, I was on foot. Because I did not have a tractor at home.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOELLER
utterances.text: And did you see Enver Hoti while you were fleeing out of the village?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: It was impossible to see everybody that day. It was chaotic. We left, we fled to save our lives. How could I see Enver Hoti that day?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOELLER
utterances.text: Thank you. There is one more issue I would like to address shortly. Dr. Hoti, earlier we talked about this person called Boski.

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOELLER
utterances.text: Did you actually see him yourself or were you told by someone else about what he did and how he looked on that day?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: I will tell you something. Until the day the -- of the offensive, Boski was very close to the Albanians. He went to Albanian homes. He was friends with him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It's a very precise question. Did you see him yourself or did somebody else tell you about his activities that day.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. We could see him ourselves from the hill.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOELLER
utterances.text: And before the burning and the looting started, how did the people who did these acts arrive in the village?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: They came in two buses from Prizren, stopped at the entrance of Krusa, at a grocery store. They stayed there for about an hour, went inside that shop. They ate there and then they went into the village. But they came in those buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOELLER
utterances.text: And when these buses arrived, were there still tanks on the main road?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: Yes. They were there. They were stationed there. They did not move from the places where they were stationed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOELLER
utterances.text: And which road did these buses take to come into the village?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: There is only one road from Prizren. There is only one road from Prizren to Orahovac. There is no other road.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOELLER
utterances.text: And is this the main road you talked about where you saw the tanks and the other vehicles?

utterances.speaker: ALI HOTI
utterances.text: Yes, yes. This main road.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOELLER
utterances.text: No further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Moeller. Dr. Hoti, that completes your evidence. Thank you for coming again to the Tribunal to give it and expand upon what you said before and explain the various things that you've been asked. You're now free to leave. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We will resume at 9.00 tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
